newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up at 16-month high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up at 16-month high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2971 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2990 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, with China trade surplus increasing in September, dealers said.
The official media on Tuesday said China had a trade surplus of $3.2 billion in September, up from $3.0 billion in August.
Dealers said the better trade status increased the supply of U.S. dollars and helped to push the yuan to close at a 16-month high. The new previous high was 8.2959 set on June 8, 1995.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2978 and fell to an intra-day low of 8.2995 early in trading. It rose to move around 8.2980 and hit a high of 8.2968 several minutes before the close.
Trading was more active than Monday with most done at 8.2980, traders said.
"As expected, China's trade surplus in September grew further, which strengthened the uptrend of the local unit," said one dealer.
Dealers expect the yuan to continue rising steadily on Wednesday.
The yuan ended up at 7.4222 from 7.4314 against 100 Japanese yen and down slightly at 1.0733 from 1.0731 against the Hong Kong dollar.
